reason: The text demonstrates that Yahweh has empathy for both leaders and people. While David (the leader) receives direct communication and opportunity to repent, the passage explicitly shows God's compassion for the people: (1) God relents from destroying Jerusalem when He 'sees' the destruction occurring (וּכְהַשְׁחִ֗ית רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם עַל־ הָֽרָעָ֔ה), (2) God commands the destroying angel to stop his hand, (3) David's prayer explicitly asks God's judgment to fall on him rather than 'your people' (וּֽבְעַמְּךָ לֹ֥א לְמַגֵּפָֽה), and (4) God accepts David's sacrifice specifically to stop the plague afflicting the people. The text portrays Yahweh showing mercy and restraint toward the nation as a whole, not indifference to their suffering.
